scope: Complete six-page supplied main, five figures, unnumbered DLS result block, four equations and 33-reference bibliography; SI and cited full articles unreviewed.

bibliographic_scope.title: Nanocrystal Surface Structure Analysis by Analytical Ultracentrifugation
bibliographic_scope.authors: Helmut Cölfen; Shay Tirosh; Arie Zaban

DLS result block.scope: Volume-weighed DLS averages as printed; plus/minus statistic not defined. Analytical pH states, not extra syntheses.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 5, Unnumbered DLS result block

synthesis_scope.common_charge: Each reported aliquot: 11.5 mL titanium(IV) isopropoxide (99.9%) in 11.5 mL dry 2-propanol, into 15.4 mL acid solution. The acid volume is solution volume, not neat acid.
synthesis_scope.common_schedule: Ambient-temperature aging for 12 h, 82 °C for 2 h to evaporate 2-propanol, then titanium-autoclave treatment for 13 h.
synthesis_scope.prior_method: Reference 8 is cited for the prior standard method; this main supplies the above actual conditions. The cited full paper is unreviewed.

analytical_preparation.transfer: Extensive basic-water washing cycles followed by nitric acid; transfer into 0.1 N HNO3 at pH 1. Base identity in the wash is not given.
analytical_preparation.pH_adjustment: NaOH adjusts analytical solution pH; amount/concentration unreported.
analytical_preparation.concentration_scope: Study-wide low-concentration range; no exact sample-specific loading or final volume.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Colloid Synthesis and Colloid Characterization

characterization_methods.TEM: JEOL, 100 kV; thin amorphous-carbon-coated copper grids. Count 140 particles for each sample, repeated at three additional areas; no pooled count inferred.
characterization_methods.XRD: Rigaku 2028, Cu Kα; Scherrer formula using [101] peak broadening.

AUC.centerpieces: 12 mm charcoal-filled Epon, chosen for low pH
AUC.optics: Online Rayleigh interference and scanning UV–vis absorption, 200–800 nm
AUC.analysis: SEDFIT least-squares g(s*) method; distributions not corrected for diffusion broadening.

source_series.Figure5b_size_basis: Calculated from the sedimentation coefficients using bulk anatase density 3.84 g/mL. Individual curve points were not digitized. Horizontal lines show TEM/XRD primary dimensions.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figures 3–5 and surrounding text

hydration_model.classification: Author model, not measured solid density or physical core-shell synthesis
assumptions: Hard spheres; charge contribution neglected under low concentration/high ionic strength.
Spherical anatase core and hydration-water shell; shell density 10% above free water.
Simple core/shell model is explicitly not correct for aggregates; shape and hydration cannot be separated by AUC alone.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 5–6, Equation 4, final model list and limitations

DLVO_and_equations.scope: Source theoretical interpretation only; no independently validated model execution.

equations.topic: van der Waals attraction for particles of radius r

equations.source_notation: psi = psi0 exp(-kappa x) = B psi0, as displayed; surrounding text defines a factor 1.7 relating surface and zeta potentials. No equation repair or execution.

DLVO_and_equations.Hamaker_scope: Rutile in water, assumed similar for anatase; not measured for these batches.
DLVO_and_equations.conclusion: For B=1.7 the source calculation predicts net attraction without a repulsive barrier at pH 1 and across the investigated pH range.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 5, Equations 1–4 and theoretical discussion

prior_surface_work.citation: A. Zaban, S. T. Aruna, S. Tirosh, B. A. Gregg, Y. Mastai, J. Phys. Chem. B 2000, 104, 4130.
prior_surface_work.scope: The introductory reference context mentions a threefold [101]-facet fraction difference, a >150 °C transformation-temperature change and solar-cell performance effects. These are prior-work observations, not newly measured values for current sample-bound records.

prior_work_and_references.future_method: Fl-FFF combined with AUC is proposed; no extra experiment or synthesis record.

source_interpretation.text: The study deliberately changes acid identity, initial pH and hydrothermal temperature to obtain two anatase colloids with similar primary sizes. Sample 1 uses acetic acid at pH 2 and 280 °C; sample 2 uses nitric acid at pH 1.9 and 250 °C. The authors interpret later solution-behavior differences in terms of surface structure; the prior facet study is cited, not independently remeasured here.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, 6, Introduction, Colloid Synthesis and surface discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Each size method describes a different object or estimator
source_interpretation.text: TEM reports number-average projected particle dimensions; XRD reports volume-average coherent crystallite sizes. DLS measures solvated, aggregated hydrodynamic dimensions. AUC sizes calculated using bulk anatase density and later hydration-model core sizes are derived interpretations, not interchangeable direct particle measurements.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–5, Figures 1–5 and DLS/model discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Analytical pH reveals different aggregation responses
source_interpretation.text: Both samples are already aggregated at pH 1 according to the authors. Sample 2 shows strong aggregation between pH 1.96 and 1.99, whereas sample 1 follows a different sedimentation trend despite similar zeta potentials below the point of zero charge. These pH settings characterize the prepared colloids; they do not create extra synthesis recipe–structure pairs.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–5, Figures 3–5 and DLS block

source_interpretation.topic: Hydration shells are a qualified model
source_interpretation.text: The authors combine DLS and AUC under hard-sphere and negligible-charge assumptions to infer an apparent hydrated density. Their spherical anatase-core/water-shell illustration is explicitly inadequate for aggregates, and shape cannot be separated from hydration using AUC alone. The last model row is printed as sample 1 at pH 1.96 although related DLS/density and conclusion statements concern sample 2; the assignment remains unresolved.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 5–6, Equation 4, model list and limitations

source_interpretation.topic: A future combined method is not a performed experiment
source_interpretation.text: Flow field-flow fractionation coupled to AUC is proposed as future work to disentangle size, shape, hydration and charge distributions. It is not an additional demonstrated preparation or measurement series in this contribution.
